scope: Bounded existing-source T4 hold reassessment only

dispositions.finding: The >0.5 m soil-depth condition is explicit. Neither limiting layer nor bedrock endpoint is identified. A 'soil depth' alias on soil_depth_to_bedrock does not establish equivalence. Construction ditch depth is separate.
dispositions.remaining_action: Retain literal >0.5 m in inventory and approved bund-slope context. Resolve a generic/effective-soil-depth definition through ontology governance or obtain verified source measurement detail; no forced bedrock claim.

evidence.quote:
Level/graded soil bunds ﬁt in well-drained and deep (> 0.5 m) soil with a slope of up to
30%.

dispositions.finding: Graded bunds explicitly discharge excess runoff in >1400 mm/year areas. The high-rainfall interpretation is confirmed on p.10, but this does not authorize assignment to a rainwater-retaining family.
dispositions.remaining_action: Keep the drainage-practice referral pending a separate family decision. The approved level-bund rainfall and slope claims remain unchanged.

evidence.quote:
Graded soil bunds are constructed following similar procedures to the level soil bunds
but having a gradient of about 1% between bund and contour line. Built in high rainfall
(> 1400 mm year−1) areas with poorly draining soil and designed to discharge excess
surface runoﬀ.

dispositions.finding: Table 1 describes graded bunds on poorly draining soil, then says level/graded bunds fit well-drained soils. Discussion confirms waterlogging risk and discharge function, but does not resolve that categorical conflict.
dispositions.remaining_action: Retain both contexts. Do not create a soil-drainage direction or universal class rule from this review; cited-primary clarification is needed if pursued.

dispositions.finding: SYI and morphometric rankings prioritize erosion intervention. p.7 calls weights arbitrary; p.14 reports selected dams on stream orders 3–5, not an exclusion rule for all other orders.
dispositions.remaining_action: No further source reading is needed to reject conversion of these particular ranks/site outcomes into establishment cutoffs. Preserve the page-linked method referral; do not invent T4 values.

dispositions.finding: Microcatchment feasibility depends on natural surfaces, soil, catchment/basin dimensions and pistachio demand. p.10 uses 91/200 mm example climates; p.11 uses 7 cubic metres transpiration as design criterion; p.14 calls 250 square metres insufficient in the extremely arid scenario. None supplies a generic rainfall cutoff.
dispositions.remaining_action: Retain the crop-specific design referral with its conditions. No further generic threshold extraction justified; any future model use requires an explicit crop/design modelling task, not approval of an invented aridity envelope.

dispositions.finding: The source concerns jessr/jessour and olive crop-water design. CCR 7.4 at assumed rainfall 235 mm depends on runoff assumptions. Source comparisons of CCR differ; they are not annual-rainfall suitability classes. Existing FAM explicitly places jessour in parked spate irrigation.
dispositions.remaining_action: Keep parked and retain the design pointer. No reassignment from the queue's microcatchment label and no new user decision requested by this audit.

dispositions.finding: Mapped organic soils at 250 m select the land-rent input footprint because they may have been waterlogged. This neither certifies former wetlands nor defines SOC concentration/peat presence; the mask is not established for all five indicators.
dispositions.remaining_action: Retain the raw organic-soil category and Greve et al. attribution. A semantically matching category and proxy scope decision would be needed; do not map it to SOC or silently extend its footprint.

dispositions.finding: The study explicitly calls itself national/regional catchment screening; p.12 reserves specific site selection for hydrology, soils and land-use investigation. Five policy/benefit indicators are priorities, not establishment-response functions.
dispositions.remaining_action: Preserve existing priority inventory. No effect or operational extraction; no T4 structural curves.

dispositions.finding: Restoration increments are distributed by current wetland location and isolated/riparian proportions. Native pp.5/10 resolve what the rule means: a composite scenario allocation, not a scalar establishment variable or existing-wetland hard mask. Approved compatible-cover evidence is a separate record and remains accepted.
dispositions.remaining_action: Preserve a method referral. Do not force into distance_to_waterbody, forest cover or a patch-area threshold. Any future use needs a deliberately specified allocation method.
